_note: v2 hook overrides for l'Atelier des Couleurs & Formes (B04_atelier_couleurs): only where the painted scene differs from the source hook.

fr_blanc_adj.hook: "BLANK!" (BLAHN): a young painter in a WHITE smock points his brush at a totally BLANK, snow-WHITE canvas on its easel.
fr_blanc_adj.why: The painting shows the blank canvas on an easel rather than held up.

fr_vert_adj.hook: A VERY ("VEHR") GREEN frog sits on top of a big tin of GREEN paint that drips VERY green down the sides.
fr_vert_adj.why: The painted frog has no wellies; the green drips on the tin are shown instead.

fr_brun_adj.hook: "BRUN-ch!" (BRUHN): a BROWN teddy bear at BRUNCH holds up a plate with a chocolate-BROWN bun.
fr_brun_adj.why: The teddy holds the plate; there is no little table.

fr_forme_noun.hook: Sounds like "form" (FORM): a girl pats a big heap of white FOAM into SHAPES: FOAM FORMS!
fr_forme_noun.why: The painting shows one heap of foam being shaped, not a separate star, heart and ball.

fr_ligne_noun.hook: The girl LEANS forward as she walks beside the long purple LINE painted on the floor: LEENY = lean-y.
fr_ligne_noun.why: The painting shows a girl leaning beside a purple line on the attic floor, not a tightrope.

fr_coin_noun.hook: Not a coin: coin (KWAN) is a CORNER. A puppy sits on a big round gold coin in the CORNER of the attic.
fr_coin_noun.why: The puppy sits on the coin in the corner.

fr_symbole_noun.hook: "SAND BOWL" (san-BOL): a boy draws a heart SYMBOL with a little stick in a bowl of sand.
fr_symbole_noun.why: The painted boy uses a stick, not a finger.

fr_grandeur_noun.hook: A tiny girl clutches her head and gapes "GRAN-DUH!" ("grahn-DUHR") up at a potted sunflower much taller than her: such SIZE, such GREATNESS.
fr_grandeur_noun.why: The painting shows a little girl, not a granny.

fr_tonne_noun.hook: TON: a little mouse in a red strongman leotard hoists two black iron weights as if each weighed a whole TONNE.
fr_tonne_noun.why: The painted leotard is plain red, not striped.

fr_regulier_adj.hook: Like "regular", said ray-gew-LYAY: a boy marches over footprints spaced perfectly evenly, one REGULAR step at a time.
fr_regulier_adj.why: The painted boy has no drum.

fr_centimetre_noun.hook: "SANTA-metre" ("sahn-tee-MEHTR"): SANTA kneels by a long yellow ruler and measures it one CENTIMETRE at a time.
fr_centimetre_noun.why: The painted Santa kneels beside the ruler rather than tiptoeing along it; the ruler has no numbers.

fr_violet_adj.hook: Vyoh-LEH: a boy in a VIOLET suit plays a PURPLE violin, bowing one last high "LEH!" note.
fr_violet_adj.why: The painting shows a violet suit and a small violin rather than a jumper and a viola.

fr_marron_adj.hook: Not "maroon": marron (mah-ROHN) means chestnut BROWN; a boy pushes a cart heaped with shiny brown chestnuts.
fr_marron_adj.why: The painted chestnuts are carried in a handcart; nothing is being roasted.

fr_multiple_adj.hook: "MULTI-PILE!" (mewl-TEEPL): a tall PILE of MANY identical blue tins, tin on tin on tin, stands in the meadow.
fr_multiple_adj.why: The painting is outdoors, so the pile stands in the meadow rather than reaching a ceiling.

fr_mixte_adj.hook: Like English 'mixed', said MEEKST: a MEEK kitten with MIXED patches of colour sits shyly beside the paint pots.
fr_mixte_adj.why: The kitten sits beside the pots rather than hiding behind them.

fr_emeraude_noun.hook: "EMERALD ROAD" (eh-muh-ROHD): a young jeweller with a magnifier lays a little ROAD of glowing green EMERALDS across green velvet.
fr_emeraude_noun.why: The painted jeweller is a young boy.

fr_pourtour_noun.hook: "POUR on TOUR" ("pour-TOOR"): a boy POURS a trail of white sand on a TOUR all the way round the OUTER EDGE of a circle.
fr_pourtour_noun.why: Respelling changed from poor-TOOR so it never reads as 'poo'; the hook is otherwise unchanged.

fr_pourpre_noun.hook: "POOR PR-incess!" (POURPR): an old seamstress, pins in her mouth, mutters as she pins a royal PURPLE gown onto the mannequin.
fr_pourpre_noun.why: Respelling changed from POORPR so it never reads as 'poo'; the hook is otherwise unchanged.

fr_sphere_noun.hook: Like English 'sphere', said SFEHR: a big glossy blue glass SPHERE hangs on a string from the attic beam, perfectly round whichever way it turns.
fr_sphere_noun.why: relocated from ciel; painted in the attic of shapes
